question: A merchant placed on display some dresses, each with a marked price. He then posted a sign “\(\dfrac13\) off on these dresses.” The cost of the dresses was \(\dfrac34\) of the price at which he actually sold them. Then the ratio of the cost to the marked price was:
solution:
A discount of \(\frac13\) leaves \(1-\frac13=\frac23\) of the marked price. Let \(M>0\) be the total marked price of the dresses. Their actual selling price was therefore \(\frac23M\).

The cost was \(\frac34\) of that selling price, so it was
\[
\frac34\left(\frac23M\right)=\frac12M.
\]
Dividing by the positive marked price \(M\), the ratio of cost to marked price is \(\frac12\), choice A.

nodes.description: Interpret the product (a/b) × q as a parts of a partition of q into b equal parts; equivalently, as the result of a sequence of operations a × q ÷ b. edges.reason: The integer-multiplier case supplies a useful stepping stone and repeated-addition interpretation. The product-of-numerators/product-of-denominators rule follows directly from a part-of-a-part area model without executing the earlier decimal-free integer-multiplier procedure; Gemini confuses this customary progression with necessity.

The endpoint provides explicit quantity-modeling experience that can help translate a fraction-of-a-whole story into an expression. Price and speed formulas do not define a fractional part, so the benefit is preparation only. This final scoped judgment does not treat a prior native acceptance of Claude's rejection as an accepted dependency.
edges.scope: Prior experience representing total, part and multiplicative relationships in application problems

edges.reason: Taking a fraction of a fractional quantity contains a fraction-by-fraction product in the full application repertoire.

Fraction division prepares ratio values with fractional terms. The target expressly permits a simple ratio, and a whole-number pair such as 6 to 3 needs only ordinary division; no fraction-by-fraction division is universal.
The target states a discount as a percent of the original and computes that amount, directly containing the percent-of-a-number operation.
edges.scope: computing discounted price as a percent of original
